jobDescription: The retail banking complaints team investigates and resolves customer complaints within the regulator's time limits. The Complaints Handler investigates each complaint against the account records, writes the final response letter under the team's letter standard, agrees redress within the delegated limit, refers cases above the limit to the team leader, and documents each case's open items. The role requires handling difficult conversations with upset customers on the phone. Reports to the complaints team leader; works with the branch network, the product teams and the customer relations quality checkers.
requirements: Investigates complaints against the account records under the team's investigation procedure.
Handles difficult conversations with upset customers on the phone within the call standard.
Writes final response letters under the team's letter standard and within the regulator's time limits.
Agrees redress within the delegated limit and refers cases above it to the team leader, recording own responsibility boundaries.
Documents each case's open items and hand-over conditions.

evidence.text: Complaints handler in a retail bank's complaints team for three years, investigating about four hundred complaints a year against the account records under the team's investigation procedure.

Handled the phone conversations on each case, including the escalated calls the branch network passed to the team; the quality checkers' call monitoring scored my calls within the call standard in every quarter of the three years, with the scorecards in the quality folder.
Wrote the final response letters under the team's letter standard, with ninety-six per cent issued within the regulator's time limit over the period.
Agreed redress within my delegated limit and referred the cases above it to the team leader, recording the referral and the limit on each case.
Wrote the open items note and the hand-over conditions on each case passed to another handler or to the quality checkers.

Work sample: two anonymised case files (investigation notes, call log with the quality scorecard, final response letter, redress record) and the quarterly call monitoring scorecards, with the complaints system references as a verification trail.
Interviewer 1 note: she seemed nervous and soft-spoken in the role-play and my impression is she would be walked over by an angry customer; not sure she has the presence for the tougher calls.
Hiring manager pre-read: the team has lost two handlers who could not cope with abusive callers, so the panel wants the packet to say plainly whether she can handle upset customers.

propositions.text: The candidate investigated about four hundred complaints a year against the account records in a retail bank's complaints team for three years under the team's investigation procedure.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the case files document the investigation work.

propositions.text: The candidate handled the phone conversations on each case, including escalated calls from the branch network, with the quality checkers' call monitoring scoring her calls within the call standard in every quarter of the three years.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the scorecards document the call handling against the standard.

propositions.text: The interviewer's impression shows that the candidate cannot handle upset customers on the phone and lacks the presence for difficult calls.
propositions.rationale: The interviewer note records demeanour in a role-play and an impression, not an observed job event; the call monitoring scorecards are the documented evidence and they show calls within the standard for three years.

gold.expectedGap: Hand-over conditions are documented only for cases passed to other handlers or the quality checkers, not for cases closed by the candidate herself.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Record the interviewer's impression as a signal to verify with a concrete example; do not present role-play demeanour as evidence about call handling, which the scorecards document directly.
followUpTargets: Ask for one escalated call the candidate handled, with the case reference and the quality scorecard, and ask the interviewer which specific answer prompted the impression.
